input.quote: Ono shall have the right, in accordance with this Section 2.2, to grant sublicenses under the Array Patents and Array Know-How to its Affiliates and to Third Parties, provided that Ono shall not engage a Third Party as either (i) a Sublicensee of the Product, or (ii) as a distributor of the Product, without Array's prior written consent.
input.rationale: The grant meets the preferred position on its material terms. Sections 2.1(a)-(c) grant us exclusive Development and Commercialization licences in the Ono Territory plus a worldwide non-exclusive Manufacturing licence, each with sublicensing rights; Section 2.2(a) expressly permits sublicensing to our Affiliates without consent, and Section 2.1(b) confirms the manufacturing licence "may be extended by Ono to Third Party manufacturers for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf" (with the Section 1.57 Subcontractor definition contemplating our use of subcontractors generally). The licences are not revocable at Array's discretion: Article 13 allows Array to terminate only for uncured material breach (90 days / 60 days for payment) or insolvency, and on expiry Section 13.1 converts our licences into "non-exclusive, fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights." Section 18.9 permits assignment without Array's consent to an acquirer of substantially all of our business or assets, and the Agreement inures to the benefit of successors and permitted assigns. The only sub-preferred features are Array's consent gate over Third Party Sublicensees/distributors and consent (not unreasonably withheld) for intra-group assignment — customary in pharma collaborations and not material enough to redline, particularly as Affiliate sublicensing and M&A succession are already free of consent. Grant-Back in Section 2.6 runs from us to Array but is limited to Improvements/Joint IP and subject to our exclusive rights, so it does not cut back the inbound grant.
